Mayon Volcano

Mayon Volcano, the Philippines' most active volcano, is famed for its perfect cone and dramatic eruption history.

Overview

Mayon (Bulakan Mayon) is an active stratovolcano in Albay, Bicol, rising 2,463 m above sea level. Its symmetric cone makes it a natural landmark and a popular tourist destination, declared a national park in 1938 and part of the Albay Biosphere Reserve.

  • Location: Albay, Philippines
  • Height: 2,463 m (8,081 ft)
  • Declared national park: July 20 1938
Timeline

Eruption History

Mayon has erupted repeatedly since the 17th century, with major events shaping local history.

  1. 1616First recorded eruption
  2. 1814Catastrophic eruption buried Cagsawa, ~1,200 deaths
  3. 1993Explosive eruption caused evacuations
  4. 2000Eruption displaced 14,114 families

Tourism & Safety

Visitors are drawn to the volcano’s perfect cone, but PHIVOLCS monitors activity and issues alerts. Safe viewing areas and guided tours are available when the alert level is low.

02

03

Conservation

Mayon sits within the Mayon Volcano Natural Park, part of the Albay Biosphere Reserve. Ongoing efforts protect its ecosystems and promote sustainable tourism.

01

UNESCO biosphere reserve since 2016

02

Reforestation projects on slopes

03

Community education on volcanic hazards

Mayon is not only a natural wonder but a cultural symbol for the Bicolanos.
